jobs.occupation: Professor of Shared Decision-making and Professional Development (combined position)
jobs.description:
Professor of Shared Decision-making and Professional Development 

A combined position as Professor (50%) and as Research Director (50%) is vacant at the Department of Regional Health Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) and at the Centre for Shared Decision Making, Lillebaelt Hospital, Vejle, respectively.

The position is offered for five years, with the possibility of extension.

The academic position
The professor will advance research into shared decision-making (SDM) and the involvement of patients and their relatives, as well as the professional development required to integrate these approaches into clinical practice. The professor will be part of the management team at the joint centre at Lillebælt Hospital and will foster coherence between research, education and implementation. The professor will be appointed at the Department of Regional Health Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, SDU. The academic field combines SDM with professional development for healthcare professionals. Interdisciplinary research and collaboration across clinical settings are expected and central to the position.

Research leadership and responsibilities
At Lillebaelt Hospital, the professor/appointee will serve as Research Director. Together with the Centre Director, the Research Director forms the joint center leadership. The Research Director has line management responsibility for academic staff and overall scientific and strategic responsibility for research activities associated with the Center for Shared Decision Making (CFFB) and the Center for Involvement of Relatives (CEPI). The two leadership roles work closely together on the development of the centers.

The professor is expected responsible for:

• 
Strategic Research Leadership and Centre Management
The position as professor includes overall scientific and strategic responsibility for the research units affiliated with both CFFB and CEPI as well as their interdisciplinary research group. This includes line management and academic leadership of researchers, ensuring the stable operation of the centers, and maintaining strategic oversight of the centers’ grant portfolio and funding pipeline.

• 
Fundraising and External Research Funding
The professor is expected to secure substantial external research funding from national and international funding bodies to ensure the long-term sustainability and development of the centers’ research activities.

• 
Practice-Oriented Empirical Research
The professor is expected to develop and lead empirical research SDM projects with a particular focus on the perspectives of patients, relatives, and healthcare professionals within different diseases, specialties and healthcare settings, while contributing to the advancement of qualitative and applied research methodologies such as action research.

• 
Development of Educational Resources, Curriculum Design, and Educational Transformation
The position requires designing and developing practical educational tools and implementation resources — e.g., learning materials — that support healthcare professionals’ learning and continuing professional development in clinical practice performing SDM.

• 
Teaching, lecturing, supervising and disseminating knowledge
The professor should teach and mentor postdocs, PhD students, and undergraduate students. Participation in assessment work is part of the position. Additionally, profiling this research area in the public eye will be an important task.

Research activity, network and collaboration
The candidate is expected to demonstrate prior experience with research activities in terms of networks and collaborations. The professor is expected to increase research activity at the research unit and to expand collaboration with other researchers at hospitals in the Region of Southern Denmark, at SDU, the rest of Denmark and internationally.

The position as Research Director at the Centre for Shared Decision Making (CFFB)
The Professorship in Shared Decision-making and Professional Development at the Center for Shared Decision Making, Vejle, Denmark, is established to support the continued implementation of Lillebaelt Hospital’s research strategy and the hospital’s overarching commitment to placing the patient at the center of care.

Over the past decade, the Center has conducted research on evidence-based approaches to SDM and has demonstrated that SDM is associated with high patient satisfaction and improved adherence to agreed treatment plans. The professorship will build on this strong research foundation by advancing knowledge on the implementation of SDM and the continuing professional development of healthcare professionals. International research consistently shows that achieving sustained and authentic SDM practice in everyday clinical care remains a significant implementation challenge. Changing professional practices and departmental cultures requires more than time-limited projects or implementation initiatives. Sustainable integration of SDM depends on ongoing and continuous competence development that supports long-term changes in clinical practice.

This professorship is positioned at the intersection of health sciences research, implementation in clinical practice, and professional development through applied educational research. The core purpose of the position is to strengthen and transform the healthcare system’s capacity for meaningful patient and family involvement through SDM.

The professorship requires strategic research leadership from a scholar with extensive expertise in lifelong learning, learning theory, curriculum theory, and action research, and with the ability to translate this knowledge into continuing professional development for healthcare professionals. The professor is expected to lead the national and international research agenda on how SDM can be integrated meaningfully and sustainably into routine clinical practice, to achieve enduring behavioral change among healthcare professionals.

Qualifications
The required qualifications:

• 
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent post-graduate research qualification and demonstrate scientific achievements at a level appropriate for appointment as Professor.

• 
The position calls for expertise in educational science as applied to the professional development of healthcare staff or other types of welfare staff, together with substantial knowledge of and research contributions to SDM.

• 
The applicant should be able to demonstrate experience of teaching and lecturing at university and postgraduate level, as well as experience as principal supervisor on PhD projects and academic assessment work, as evidenced by the teaching portfolio.

• 
Danish language skills are not required at the time of appointment, but must be mastered at proficiency level C1, at the Common European Framework of References for Languages within the first 2 years of employment.

The ideal candidate preferably demonstrates:

• 
The candidate should demonstrate experience with leadership capacity with the ability to lead research teams, drive cultural change, and contribute strategically to the development of the centers.

• 
The candidate holds experience in research management, interdisciplinary collaboration, and attraction of external funding for professional development and/or SDM-oriented activities will be considered an advantage.

• 
The candidate preferably demonstrates experience with practice-oriented empirical research. Research that is aimed at both an international research community, and ideally also at the target group of professionals in Denmark; therefore, publications and outputs are welcome to be in Danish – whether in the form of books, leaflets, journal publications or other material designed to ensure that both professionals undertaking continuing professional development in Denmark and students on undergraduate program are best supported and thereby ensuring impact.

• 
The candidate has prior experience with developing, implementing, and/or evaluating educational programs, frameworks, and curricula for continuing professional development, preferably in terms of SDM-related competencies. Experience of developing and evaluating continuing professional education in clinical settings is valued.

• 
The preferred candidate can motivate and supervise, has proven research management skills, good interpersonal skills in charge of a research group, and has a clear vision for how to further strengthen the research unit at CFFB as strong interpersonal and collaborative skills are essential.

• 
The successful applicant will have documented experience of leading research and researchers, obtain external funding and work across disciplines and organizations.

Employers
CFFB is a national knowledge and competence center based at Lillebaelt Hospital. Since 2014, it has researched SDM and since 2019 developed approaches for implementation in clinical practice. CEPI works to strengthen meaningful involvement of relatives. The centers retain their distinct areas of responsibility while collaborating closely on research and practice. Lillebaelt Hospital provides somatic and mental healthcare across sites in Vejle, Kolding and Middelfart. Patient and family involvement is central to their approach to care.

SDU's Department of Regional Health Research links research and education with hospitals and clinical environments across the Region of Southern Denmark. The Department of Regional Health Research supports research in relation to the person as a whole, the good life and the more common diseases, makes out a platform for scientists and educators and builds a bridge between University of Southern Denmark, The Region of Southern Denmark, the hospitals in the region and the patient. The department focuses on the continuity of patient care across sectors, hospitals, and specialist fields.

Reference 
The professor and research director will refer to the hospital management regarding matters concerning the management of the centres, and to the Head of the Department of Regional Health Research, Mikkel Brabrand, in matters regarding the professorship.

Contact information
Further information concerning the position can be obtained by contacting:

• 
The Research Coordinator at Lillebælt Hospital, Jonna Skov Madsen, Jonna.Skov.Madsen@rsyd.dk, +45 30507825

• 
The Director of the Centre, Karina Olling, Karina.Olling@rsyd.dk, +45 51518696

• 
The Head of the Department of Regional Health Research, SDU, Mikkel Brabrand, mbrabrand@health.sdu.dk, +45 93534980

Salary and terms of employment
The successful applicant for the professor position will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Professor is salaried in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and on terms corresponding to salary grade 37 of the Danish state salary system. Additional qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Center for Shared Decision Making (Center for Fælles Beslutningstagning), Beriderbakken 4, 7100 Vejle, Denmark.

Application
Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
An application

• 
A detailed CV

• 
Degree certificates (inclusive of Ph.D.-diploma or equivalent)

• 
A complete and numbered list of publications

• 
10 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position (please notice that one pdf file must be attached for each publication)

• 
It is permitted to merge the 10 scientific peer-reviewed publications into a single PDF file due to upload constraints.

• 
A teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
Track record in obtaining research funding

• 
National and international research collaboration and collaborations with researchers in other disciplines and sectors

• 
A research plan detailing the candidate’s ideas and plans for her/his future research work

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application. Incomplete applications with regards to the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

The application deadline is 11 November 2026 at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST)

Assessment
Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Real World Evidence for Knee Osteoarthritis
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to help advance PROBE, an Innovative Health Initiative (IHI) public-private partnership focused on patient-relevant osteoarthritis endpoints using big data. You will be anchored in Novo Nordisk’s R&D Real World Evidence (RWE) area, with access to its scientific expertise and support network, and work closely with our Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) team and partners across the consortium.

Your main research focus will be PROBE Work Package 4 (WP4): analysing patient characteristics and identifying factors (such as clinical variables and biomarkers) associated with osteoarthritis progression, meaningful patient subgroups, and potential surrogates of clinically relevant outcomes. You will also help establish the infrastructure and authorised access needed for analysis in the federated database network and contribute to deliverables across other work packages.

What you'll bring

You have a PhD in epidemiology, biostatistics, data science, biomedical informatics, computational biology, public health, or a related field, together with experience analysing complex health data. We expect you to bring:

• 
Strong programming and reproducible analysis skills in R or Python, knowledge of modern machine learning/AI methods, and sound statistical reasoning.

• 
Experience with observational, registry, electronic health record, clinical, or other longitudinal patient-level datasets.

• 
The ability to formulate research questions, assess data fitness, interpret results responsibly, and explain findings to both technical and nontechnical colleagues.

• 
The organisation and initiative to move collaborative research forward across teams and institutions, with fluent written and spoken English.

• 
Experience in osteoarthritis or musculoskeletal research, patient stratification, biomarker research, distributed or federated analytics, and health-data governance would be an advantage.

You do not need experience in every area to apply.

What you'll do

• 
Design and conduct reproducible analyses of patient demographics, clinical characteristics, disease burden, and longitudinal outcomes across relevant osteoarthritis datasets.

• 
Investigate prognostic variables, patterns of disease progression, patient subgroups, treatment effectiveness, and candidate biomarkers or surrogate outcomes in support of relevant research questions.

• 
Work with data owners, WP3 infrastructure partners, internal data specialists, and governance teams to help establish data connections, permissions, harmonised definitions, and practical access to the federated database network.

• 
Apply appropriate statistical and machine-learning methods to heterogeneous real-world data, documenting assumptions, data quality, limitations, and validation results.

• 
Translate findings into scientific reports, presentations, publications, and consortium deliverables, including contributions to other areas where your analyses are relevant.

• 
Coordinate closely with the R&D RWE team and PPP team, and communicate progress and results to multidisciplinary public and private partners.

Who you'll work with

Within R&D RWE, you will work alongside epidemiologists and data scientists who use real-world patient data to inform disease understanding and research decisions. The PPP office will be a close partner in consortium coordination, scientific communication, and delivery of PROBE commitments.

About PROBE

Knee osteoarthritis affects people differently, making it difficult to predict progression and identify who may benefit from specific treatments. PROBE brings together patient data and expertise across academic, healthcare, industry, and patient partners to improve patient stratification, predictive models, endpoints, and clinical trial design. Its federated approach is intended to enable analysis across datasets while respecting applicable governance and privacy requirements.

Responsibilities and challenges

We are looking for a Senior Biologist to provide project-level scientific leadership for DHI MUSE and other avian ecology assignments. You will define research questions and analytical scope of projects, guide ecological interpretation, own the scientific reporting and act as external and internal stakeholders’ scientific point of contact. • Own scientific reports, technical notes, presentations and the scientific content of client proposals through internal review and client approval.

• Act as scientific point of contact in dialogue with clients, regulators, project teams, suppliers and subcontractors.

• Review scientific deliverables and proposals, respond to review comments and advise when available evidence cannot support a requested conclusion.

• Help maintain consistent scientific working practices and actively share knowledge within the team and company.

Qualifications and personal skills

We are looking for a colleague with the following qualifications:

Required:

• Master's degree or PhD in biology, ecology, ornithology or a closely related discipline, or otherwise relevant experience in ornithology.

• Substantial professional experience in ecology, environmental monitoring, ecological consultancy or a comparable applied field.

• Demonstrated experience designing ecological studies and interpreting complex, multi-source datasets.

jobs.occupation: Senior Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) wanted for strong, supportive team
jobs.description:
Design solutions that solve whole classes of problems rather than individual tasks. As a Senior SRE at Systematic, you keep the systems running that healthcare staff and patients depend on.

Would you like to shape the future of our infrastructure by designing scalable, elegant solutions that solve classes of problems rather than individual tasks? Join our skilled Site Reliability Engineering team where you’ll have the opportunity to think beyond the immediate fix and architect systems that transform how we operate at scale. Your work will keep healthcare solutions running for the clinicians and care staff who depend on them.

The job

As a Senior SRE with a systems engineering mindset, you’ll work at the intersection of deep technical expertise and strategic thinking. You’ll identify patterns across our diverse infrastructure, from Kubernetes clusters to Azure VMs, and create unified solutions that eliminate entire categories of operational toil. This isn’t about fixing one deployment pipeline; it’s about building a framework that makes all deployments reliable. This isn’t about patching one vulnerability; it’s about architecting a security posture that scales across our organization.

You’ll have access to cutting-edge technologies and the autonomy to innovate, with opportunities to work across multiple environments including our ao-admin Kubernetes cluster, Docker-based deployments, Azure-hosted infrastructure, and healthcare-focused systems. When you are ready, you will join the SRE team’s on-call rotation.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Architect automation systems that eliminate classes of manual work, thinking in terms of platforms and capabilities rather than individual scripts

• Develop infrastructure tooling that empowers development teams to self-service their operational needs while maintaining reliability standards

• Build observability frameworks that provide unified insights across diverse environments, making patterns visible and actionable

• Create abstraction layers that hide complexity while providing powerful capabilities, whether through Terraform modules, Helm charts, or custom operators

• Drive infrastructure evolution by identifying systemic improvements and leading their implementation from concept to production

• Collaborate with development teams to understand their patterns of needs and design operations-ready solutions that scale

• Mentor team members in systems thinking and architectural approaches, sharing your problem-solving methodology

• Apply best practices in site reliability engineering, advocating for solutions that improve reliability, security, and maintainability at scale

• Research and prototype emerging technologies and approaches, evaluating their fit for solving our systemic challenges

Joining the team

You’ll join one of our two skilled SRE teams, each consisting of approximately 10 professionals working from our offices in Aarhus and Bucharest. Our teams operate with a DevOps philosophy and use a mix of Scrum and Kanban methodologies depending on the project needs.

We value engineers who can see the forest and the trees, who understand both the technical details and the broader patterns. You’ll work with colleagues who manage everything from Kubernetes clusters to Windows VMs, from Terraform modules to Prometheus monitoring, and you’ll help us find the common threads that allow us to operate more efficiently and reliably.

This is a role with significant room to manoeuvre and influence. You’ll have the opportunity to work with the newest technologies while solving real operational challenges that impact critical systems across multiple domains. Our healthcare solutions, such as Columna, support the continuum of care across hospitals, communities and private homes, so your work contributes directly to patient safety.

Your qualifications

Our ideal candidate is someone who gets excited about patterns, who sees a specific problem and immediately starts thinking “what other problems does this represent?” You’re the engineer who, when asked to automate a deployment, designs a deployment framework. When asked to fix a monitoring gap, you create an observability strategy.

Our ideal candidate would have:

• Experience as a Senior in site reliability engineering, systems engineering, or platform engineering roles with demonstrated impact on infrastructure scalability

• Solid understanding of abstraction and design patterns in infrastructure, with experience creating reusable frameworks, modules, or platforms

• Experience with observability at scale, including metrics, logging, and tracing systems (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK stack, or similar)

• Strong communication skills to articulate architectural decisions, document systems, and mentor others in systems thinking

• Proven ability to architect solutions that solve multiple problems simultaneously, with examples of platforms or systems you’ve built

We value diverse backgrounds and encourage candidates who are passionate about systems thinking, infrastructure architecture, and solving problems at scale to apply, even if they do not meet every requirement perfectly!

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Welcome to Systematic Aarhus

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 events a year of both social and professional character. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Start your development here

jobs.occupation: Maintenance Support Professional
jobs.description:
Help secure reliable operations today — and support the transition into LEO Pharma’s future production setup.

At LEO Pharma, we go beyond the skin to make a lasting difference for people living with skin diseases. Behind that mission is a strong technical foundation, and in this role, you will help ensure that foundation is reliable, compliant and future-ready.

Join LEO Pharma in Ballerup and take on a key technical role at an exciting time of change. As Maintenance Support Professional, you will help keep critical technical installations running, support compliance-based maintenance, and contribute to the proper and structured close-down of the old factory as we prepare for a new innovative production facility to fully take over.

**

Your role**

You will provide technical support for the planning, implementation and development of maintenance across utilities, technical installations, plants and production equipment at Site Ballerup. You will act as a technical problem-solver, resolve technical issues in daily operations while also supporting larger transformation activities related to the factory transition.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Supporting day-to-day operation and availability of both the old and state of the art technical installations and equipment.

• Acting as troubleshooter on ad hoc technical assignments, breakdowns and operational challenges.

• Ensuring maintenance documentation is maintained, optimized and aligned with LEO Pharma policies and GxP requirements.

• Creating, Reviewing and technically approving documents in QMS in close collaboration with stakeholders.

• Supporting the structured close-down of the old factory and contributing to a smooth transition towards the new facility.

You will also be responsible for GxP documentation from the section, including documentation in CMMS and QMS. In addition, you will support timely follow-up on deviations, corrective actions, action items and CAPAs, and act as technical SME in root cause analysis related to deviation handling. You may also participate in relevant CAPEX projects as participant or package owner and lead smaller OPEX projects.

**

Your qualifications**

We imagine that you bring solid technical expertise, good documentation discipline and experience from a regulated environment. You are used to working across functions and can communicate clearly with colleagues and stakeholders at different levels of the organisation.

We are looking for someone with:

• An educational background as an engineer, marine engineer, process technician or equivalent.

• 5+ years’ experience with maintenance of utilities, technical installations, plants or production equipment.

• Hands-on experience with deviation handling, root cause analysis, CAPAs or similar processes.

• Knowledge of GxP, technical documentation and regulated quality processes.

• Experience with CMMS systems such as PEMAC and quality systems such as Veeva Quality is an advantage.

• Experience with RCM (Reliability Centered Maintenance) is an advantage.

As a person, you are proactive, structured and solution-oriented. You enjoy troubleshooting, can manage several tasks at the same time, and are motivated by collaborating across departments to find practical and compliant solutions. You communicate with confidence, build trust with stakeholders and contribute to a positive, LEAN-oriented culture. Working with an optimisation perspective and a focus towards improvements.

**

Your new team**

You will join Maintenance Support at Site Ballerup. We are a team that plays an important role in securing stable technical operations and compliant maintenance. We work closely with Operational Maintenance, Engineering, production areas and laboratories, and we support both daily operations and strategic site changes. Together, we are helping LEO Pharma close one chapter in a responsible way while preparing for the next generation of innovative production.

**

Contact and application**

For additional information, please contact Adam Lundsby Rejkjaer, Senior Team Leader, Maintenance Support at BDYDK@leo-pharma.com

You do not need to upload a cover letter, but feel free to add a few sentences in your resume or CV on why this position has your interest.

Beyond the skin

Join LEO Pharma, a global leader in medical dermatology, as we go beyond the skin to make a lasting impact.  Our innovative approach sets us apart. We are dedicated to leaving a legacy that positively impacts patients, colleagues, and our planet.

At LEO Pharma, we believe in the power of individuals to drive change. Our flat organizational structure empowers you to make a visible impact and offers versatile roles for professional growth. We value diversity and welcome applications from all qualified candidates, recognizing that our different perspectives, backgrounds, and attitudes enable us to make the best decisions. Join our passionate team at LEO Pharma and be yourself as we work together to make a difference.

For certain positions, LEO Pharma might complete a background check conducted by a third party.

jobs.occupation: Senior Operational Technology (OT) Security Officer
jobs.description:
Imagine a future where you'll protect the ability to supply electricity and heat to the end user and make sure that our critical OT systems are protected against hackers

Why join?

Proven very high employee satisfaction and motivation

Continuous development opportunities for all employees

Competitive salary, pension scheme, and attractive holiday package

A wide range of health benefits, such as health insurance, nutritious food, and fitness facilities in our office locations

Join us in this role where you’ll be working as a Senior Operational Technology (OT) Security Officer to strengthen the security, resilience, and compliance of Ørsted Bioenergy. In this role, you will act as a trusted security lead across OT, IT, engineering, and operations, helping protect critical systems while enabling safe, reliable, and efficient operations. Further more we are partnering with operations, engineering, maintenance, IT, and third-party vendors to ensure security controls are practical, risk-based, and compatible with operational safety and availability – and we “translate” technical cyber risk into clear business, safety, and operational impact requirements. We operate in complex, multi-site, international, or safety-critical operational environments.

**Welcome to Bioenergy

**You’ll be part of OT Security where you, together with your colleagues, will be working on Ørsted Danish powerplant. Our task is to protect the powerplants ability to produce electricity and heat against hacker attacks. So you need to understand Danish, when you’re out on the powerplants. We are a small team of 4 persons located in Jutland (Jylland) who works together and strive in helping each other in our daily tasks. As a team, we have an open and direct commutation where we discuss ideas strategy and ideas to develop and mature our solutions, so they are robust and they deal with the reality we face.

You’ll play an important role in:

• leading the development and continuous improvement of OT security governance, policies, standards, and procedures

• assessing, managing, and reducing cyber risk across OT environments, including industrial control systems, SCADA, PLCs, IIoT, and related networks

• defining and supporting secure OT architecture, including network segmentation, secure remote access, asset visibility, access control, logging, monitoring, and vulnerability management

• conducting OT security risk assessments, gap analyses, and maturity reviews aligned with recognised frameworks e.g. Danish legislation “Lov om styrket Beredskab i Energisektoren”, IEC 62443, ISO 27001 and relevant regulatory requirements

• partnering with operations, engineering, maintenance, IT, and third-party vendors to ensure security controls are practical, risk-based, and compatible with operational safety and availability requirements

• driving OT security awareness and training for technical and operational teams.

To succeed in the role, you:

• hold a relevant degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Cyber Security, Information Technology, Automation, or equivalent practical experience

• understand and know how to operate in ICS systems and possess understanding of 24/7 production environment

• are familiar with IT networks like, Purdue model, firewall, data diodes etc.

• hold knowledge about EIC 62433, ISO 27001 and "Lov om styrket Beredskab i Energisektoren" as we operate according to this legislation

• are a good team player and at the same are strong on being responsible of incl. conducting your own tasks – you need to be fluent in both Danish and English language as well due to nature our stake holder landscape

• are flexible - both in terms of taking on tasks outside your comfortzone, being curious in learning new areas and assist your team in whatever tasks are needed.

Some travel within Denmark to the different sites must be expected in the this role.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

**Send your application and CV to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

**Position salary range:

**For this position, the expected base pay range is kr55,040.00- kr82,560.00 for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Our benefits package:

**For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11 % contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3 % holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and well-being programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, and internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).
